tui.explain.common.edges.periodization: periodization — the signal repeats periodically: bands are exactly N/2ʲ long, but the edges may jump
tui.explain.common.edges.zero: zero — zeros past the ends: bands grow by (L − 1)/2 and the edges step down to zero
tui.explain.common.edges.reflect: reflect — mirroring without repeating the end sample: …, x₂, x₁ | x₀, x₁, x₂ (as pywt)
tui.explain.common.rule: How the threshold λ for the detail coefficients d₁ … d_J is chosen
tui.explain.common.rule.bayesshrink: BayesShrink — a threshold per band from the signal variance estimate λⱼ = σ²/σₓ; usually best by MSE
tui.explain.common.rule.visushrink: VisuShrink — one universal threshold σ·√(2 ln N): almost all noise goes, but the signal is oversmoothed
tui.explain.common.rule.sureshrink: SureShrink — each band's threshold minimises the SURE risk estimate; sparse bands get the universal one
tui.explain.common.rule.minimax: Minimax — the Donoho–Johnstone threshold σ·(0.3936 + 0.1829·log₂N): milder than VisuShrink
tui.explain.common.mode: How the threshold is applied: soft, hard or garrote
tui.explain.common.mode.soft: soft — values below λ are zeroed, the rest shrink towards zero by λ: smooth, but amplitudes drop
tui.explain.common.mode.hard: hard — values below λ are zeroed, the rest stay as they are: sharper peaks, but noise spikes remain
tui.explain.common.mode.garrote: garrote — the non-negative garrote y·(1 − λ²/y²): between soft and hard, large values barely change

tui.explain.matrix.op.analysis: A = [L; B]: rows of h₀ and h₁ shifted by 2 — one DWT step, A·x gives a and d

tui.explain.matrix.mode.zero: zero — zeros past the ends: each band gets ⌊(N + L − 1)/2⌋ rows, so A is not square
tui.explain.matrix.mode.period: periodization — x repeats periodically: A is square N × N, and AᵀA = I for an orthogonal bank
tui.explain.matrix.mode.symm: symmetric — x is mirrored past the edge, repeating the end sample (as pywt); A is not square
tui.explain.matrix.order: Row order: all L rows, then all B rows, or interleaved L₀, B₀, L₁, B₁, …
tui.explain.matrix.order.blocks: [L; B] — lowpass rows (output a) on top, highpass rows (output d) below
tui.explain.matrix.order.interleaved: Interleaved — L and B rows alternate: the block-Toeplitz structure with 2 × 2 blocks shows

tui.explain.matrix.cell: Cell: colour shows each entry's sign and size, numbers show values when N fits; click or c
tui.explain.matrix.row: Highlighted row: its dot product with x is on the right; ◂ ▸ or ↑↓ move to the next one

tui.explain.matrix.panel.checks: Numerical checks of the current matrix: orthogonality, PR, singular values

tui.explain.matrix.panel.sigma: Singular values σᵢ on a log₁₀ scale; σ_max/σ_min is the condition number; s returns to the matrix
tui.explain.matrix.panel.origin: Where A comes from: every second row of the Toeplitz T(h₀) is kept — that is ↓2
tui.explain.matrix.chip.legend: Cell colours: blue is positive, vermilion negative, background zero; ◂ ▸ move the row

tui.explain.matrix.check.transpose: Synthesis S against Aᵀ: they match only for an orthogonal bank
tui.explain.matrix.check.inverse: ‖S·A·x − x‖ — the reconstruction error on the test x; ≈ 0 means PR
tui.explain.matrix.check.dct: How well DCT-II diagonalises T + H: what is left off the diagonal of C(T+H)Cᵀ
tui.explain.matrix.check.levinson: Solving T(r)·x = e₁ by the Levinson–Durbin recursion in O(N²), and its relative residual
tui.explain.matrix.check.gohberg: The inverse of the Toeplitz T by the Gohberg–Semencul formula, checked as T·T⁻¹ = I
tui.explain.matrix.check.singular: Largest and smallest σ and cond = σ_max/σ_min: how much A can amplify an error

tui.explain.resample.mode: Resampling mode: downsampling ↓M, upsampling ↑L or the rational L/M
tui.explain.resample.mode.down: ↓M — keep every M-th sample: fs′ = fs/M; without a filter frequencies above fs′/2 alias
tui.explain.resample.mode.up: ↑L — insert L − 1 zeros between samples: fs′ = L·fs; without a filter spectral images remain
tui.explain.resample.mode.rational: L/M — ↑L, one anti-aliasing filter, then ↓M: fs′ = fs·L/M
tui.explain.resample.m: M — the downsampling factor; − and + change it
tui.explain.resample.l: L — the upsampling factor; < and > change it
tui.explain.resample.filter: Anti-aliasing filter — a Kaiser FIR against aliasing at ↓M and images at ↑L
tui.explain.resample.filter.on: AA on — the filter is in place: aliasing and spectral images are suppressed
tui.explain.resample.filter.bypass: Bypass — no filter: you see the spectrum copies alias or the images remain
tui.explain.resample.cutoff: Cutoff of the anti-aliasing filter as a fraction of π/max(L, M), the lower Nyquist
tui.explain.resample.source: Input signal: a tone, a sweep or the file from the Signal tab
tui.explain.resample.source.tone: Tone — a single sinusoid: easy to see where it aliases after ↓M
tui.explain.resample.source.sweep: Sweep — the frequency rises over time: aliasing shows up as a mirrored line
tui.explain.resample.source.file: File — the signal open in the Signal tab
tui.explain.resample.panel.controls: Resampling settings: mode, M and L, anti-aliasing filter and input
tui.explain.resample.panel.before: Input spectrum at fs; with the anti-aliasing filter response if it runs before ↓M
tui.explain.resample.panel.after: Spectrum after resampling at fs′; with the filter bypassed aliasing and images show
tui.explain.resample.panel.readouts: Readouts: rates before and after, filter parameters and alias suppression
tui.explain.resample.panel.time: Samples before and after: ↑L inserts L − 1 zeros, ↓M keeps every M-th
tui.explain.resample.legend.after: How many spectrum copies X((ω − 2πk)/M) add up after ↓M

tui.explain.filters.role.h1: h₁ — the analysis highpass: it produces the details d
tui.explain.filters.role.f0: f₀ — the synthesis lowpass: rebuilds the signal from a after ↑2

pipeline.about.remove_dc: Subtracts each channel's mean, removing the DC component
pipeline.param.clip.limit: Clipping level: anything beyond ±limit is cut to it
pipeline.about.quantize: Quantises the signal to a given bit depth, optionally with dither
pipeline.param.quantize.bits: Bit depth: fewer bits mean a coarser step and louder quantisation noise
pipeline.param.quantize.dither: Whether to add triangular (TPDF) noise before rounding
pipeline.param.quantize.dither.yes: TPDF dither: the error becomes steady noise unrelated to the signal
pipeline.param.quantize.dither.no: plain rounding: the error follows the signal and sounds like distortion
pipeline.param.quantize.seed: Dither generator seed; channel c uses seed + c
pipeline.about.mulaw: μ-law companding: compresses or expands the dynamic range
pipeline.param.mulaw.direction.encode: compress: y = sign(x)·ln(1 + μ|x|)/ln(1 + μ), input clipped to ±1
pipeline.param.mulaw.direction.decode: expand: the inverse map, restoring the original scale
pipeline.param.mulaw.mu: The μ parameter: larger values squeeze loud samples harder relative to quiet ones
pipeline.about.split: Splits a signal into left and right, or picks out one channel
pipeline.param.split.mode: What goes to outputs l and r
pipeline.param.split.mode.lr: l gets channel 0, r channel 1 (mono feeds channel 0 to both)
pipeline.param.split.mode.channel: both outputs get the channel numbered channel
pipeline.param.split.channel: Zero-based channel number for mode channel
pipeline.about.mixdown: Mixes all channels into one by averaging them
pipeline.about.mid_side: Rotates stereo between L/R and M/S: M = (L + R)/√2, S = (L − R)/√2
pipeline.param.mid_side.direction: Direction; the rotation is orthogonal, hence lossless
pipeline.param.mid_side.direction.encode: L/R → M/S: channel 0 becomes mid, channel 1 side
pipeline.param.mid_side.direction.decode: M/S → L/R: recovers left and right
pipeline.about.delay: Delays the signal by prepending zeros
pipeline.param.delay.samples: Delay in samples, or seconds with an s suffix (0.01s)
pipeline.about.reverse: Reverses the signal in time: the last sample comes first
pipeline.about.cut: Keeps the part of the signal in [begin, end)
pipeline.param.cut.begin: Start of the part, inclusive: samples, or seconds with an s suffix (0.01s)
pipeline.param.cut.end: End of the piece, excluded; 0 means to the end of the signal. Samples or seconds with s (0.01s)
pipeline.about.downsample: Downsampling ↓M: keeps every M-th sample, optionally removing aliasing first
pipeline.param.downsample.m: Downsampling factor M: the sample rate is divided by M
pipeline.param.downsample.attenuation_db: Alias suppression of the Kaiser filter, dB: more is cleaner but the filter is longer
pipeline.param.downsample.anti_alias: Whether to low-pass at fs/(2M) before dropping samples
pipeline.param.downsample.anti_alias.yes: Kaiser low-pass first, then every M-th sample: no aliasing
pipeline.param.downsample.anti_alias.no: just every M-th sample: content above fs/(2M) folds onto low frequencies
pipeline.param.downsample.phase: Downsampling offset: p keeps x[p], x[p+M], …; must be below M
pipeline.about.upsample: Upsampling ↑M: inserts M−1 zeros between samples, optionally removing images
pipeline.param.upsample.m: Upsampling factor M: the sample rate is multiplied by M
pipeline.param.upsample.attenuation_db: Image suppression of the Kaiser filter, dB: more is cleaner but the filter is longer
pipeline.param.upsample.anti_image: Whether to low-pass the zero-stuffed signal to remove spectral images
pipeline.param.upsample.anti_image.yes: Kaiser low-pass with gain M: a smooth interpolation of the input
pipeline.param.upsample.anti_image.no: zero stuffing only: the spectrum keeps M−1 images
pipeline.about.resample: Changes the rate by L/M: upsample ↑L, low-pass, downsample ↓M
pipeline.param.resample.l: Upsampling factor L, the numerator of the rate ratio
pipeline.param.resample.m: Downsampling factor M, the denominator: the new rate is fs·L/M
pipeline.param.resample.attenuation_db: Image and alias suppression of the Kaiser filters, dB: more is cleaner but longer
pipeline.about.convolve: Full convolution with a bank or library filter: output length N + L − 1
pipeline.param.convolve.filter: Filter as wavelet.role: h0/h1 analysis low/high-pass, f0/f1 synthesis; or a library name
pipeline.param.convolve.method: How to compute it; results match up to rounding
pipeline.param.convolve.method.auto: FFT when both operands are at least 160 samples long, else direct
pipeline.param.convolve.method.direct: direct sum of products, O(N·L): faster for short filters
pipeline.param.convolve.method.fft: via FFT, O((N+L) log(N+L)): faster for long filters
pipeline.about.dwt: Discrete wavelet transform: multilevel split into bands aJ, dJ…d1
pipeline.param.dwt.wavelet: Wavelet name (haar, db4, sym8, coif3, bior2.2, dmey…): sets the filter bank
pipeline.param.dwt.levels: Number of levels J; 0 picks the maximum for this length minus 3, at least 1
pipeline.param.dwt.ext: How the signal is extended beyond its edges; this sets the band lengths
pipeline.param.dwt.ext.symmetric: mirror repeating the edge: … x1 x0 | x0 x1 …
pipeline.param.dwt.ext.smooth: linear extrapolation from the two edge samples
pipeline.param.dwt.ext.reflect: mirror without repeating the edge: … x2 x1 | x0 x1 x2 …
pipeline.param.dwt.ext.antisymmetric: mirror with a sign flip: … −x1 −x0 | x0 x1 …
pipeline.param.dwt.ext.antireflect: point reflection about the edge sample: x[−n] = 2x0 − x[n]
pipeline.about.idwt: Inverse DWT: rebuilds the signal from bands aJ, dJ…d1
pipeline.param.idwt.wavelet: Synthesis wavelet: auto reuses the analysis one; any other name must match it
pipeline.param.idwt.ext: Edge extension: auto reuses the analysis mode; any other value must match it
pipeline.param.idwt.ext.auto: use the mode stored with the coefficients
pipeline.param.idwt.ext.symmetric: mirror repeating the edge: … x1 x0 | x0 x1 …
pipeline.param.idwt.ext.smooth: linear extrapolation from the two edge samples
pipeline.param.idwt.ext.reflect: mirror without repeating the edge: … x2 x1 | x0 x1 x2 …
pipeline.param.idwt.ext.antisymmetric: mirror with a sign flip: … −x1 −x0 | x0 x1 …
pipeline.param.idwt.ext.antireflect: point reflection about the edge sample: x[−n] = 2x0 − x[n]
pipeline.about.swt: Stationary (undecimated) wavelet transform: every band keeps the signal length
pipeline.param.swt.wavelet: Wavelet name (haar, db4, sym8, coif3, bior2.2, dmey…): sets the filter bank
pipeline.param.swt.levels: Number of levels J; 0 picks it; the signal is periodically padded to a multiple of 2^J
pipeline.param.swt.norm: Whether to divide the filters by √2 so band energy equals signal energy
pipeline.param.swt.norm.no: DWT filters as is (as in pywt): energy doubles at every level
pipeline.param.swt.norm.yes: filters ×1/√2: the total band energy equals the signal energy
pipeline.about.lift53: 5/3 (LeGall, JPEG 2000) wavelet via lifting: multilevel decomposition
pipeline.param.lift53.levels: Number of levels; the signal needs at least 2^levels samples
pipeline.param.lift53.integer: Whether to compute in integers, the reversible lossless JPEG 2000 variant
pipeline.param.lift53.integer.no: floating-point lifting: perfect reconstruction up to rounding
pipeline.param.lift53.integer.yes: samples ×32768 to integers, integer lifting: 16-bit PCM comes back exactly
pipeline.about.ilift53: Inverse 5/3 lifting: rebuilds the signal from lift53 bands, real or integer
pipeline.about.iswt: Inverse SWT: rebuilds the signal from the bands, trimmed to the input length
pipeline.param.iswt.wavelet: Synthesis wavelet: auto reuses the SWT one; any other name must match it
pipeline.about.threshold: Thresholds wavelet coefficients: shrinks the details by a rule
pipeline.param.threshold.rule: How the threshold λ is chosen per level; the approximation is left alone
pipeline.param.threshold.rule.bayes: BayesShrink: λ = σ²/σx per level, adapts to the signal
pipeline.param.threshold.rule.visu: VisuShrink: λ = σ√(2 ln N), removes nearly all noise but oversmooths
pipeline.param.threshold.rule.sure: SureShrink: λ minimises Stein's unbiased risk estimate per level
pipeline.param.threshold.rule.minimax: Donoho–Johnstone minimax threshold: milder than the universal one
pipeline.param.threshold.mode: Shrinkage function: how coefficients change relative to λ
pipeline.param.threshold.mode.soft: soft: |y| ≤ λ → 0, the rest shrink by λ; smooth but biased
pipeline.param.threshold.mode.hard: hard: |y| ≤ λ → 0, the rest kept; less bias, more residual noise
pipeline.param.threshold.mode.garrote: non-negative garrote: y − λ²/y when |y| > λ, between soft and hard
pipeline.param.threshold.levels: Which detail levels to process: J or J1..J2; 1 is the finest, d1
pipeline.param.threshold.sigma: Noise level σ: mad_d1 estimates it as median|d1|/0.6745, or give a number
pipeline.about.band_edit: Edits decomposition bands: mutes some and changes the gain of the rest
pipeline.param.band_edit.enabled: Bands to keep, comma-separated (a, d1, d3) or all; the others are zeroed
pipeline.param.band_edit.gains_db: Band gains in dB, comma-separated, like d2=-6, a=3; other bands stay as is
pipeline.about.band_energy: Report: the share of energy in each band, per channel
pipeline.about.envelope: Envelope: magnitude of the analytic signal (Hilbert transform)
pipeline.about.inst_freq: Instantaneous frequency, Hz: derivative of the analytic signal's phase
pipeline.about.cepstrum: Real cepstrum: inverse FFT of the log magnitude spectrum
pipeline.about.dct: Type-II discrete cosine transform of each channel
pipeline.about.idct: Inverse DCT (DCT-III): recovers the signal from DCT-II coefficients
pipeline.about.xcorr: Cross-correlation of signals a and b, channel by channel
pipeline.param.xcorr.mode: Which part of the correlation to output, as in numpy.correlate
pipeline.param.xcorr.mode.same: the central part, as long as input a
pipeline.param.xcorr.mode.valid: only fully overlapping lags: length |Na − Nb| + 1
pipeline.param.xcorr.normalize: Whether to divide by √(Ea·Eb) so values lie in [−1, 1]
pipeline.param.xcorr.normalize.no: raw sums of products: the scale depends on the signal levels
pipeline.param.xcorr.normalize.yes: correlation coefficient: 1 means the same shape at that lag
pipeline.about.denoise: Wavelet denoising: DWT, threshold the details, inverse DWT
pipeline.param.denoise.wavelet: Wavelet for the decomposition; long smooth ones (sym8, db8) suit smooth signals
pipeline.param.denoise.levels: Number of levels J; 0 picks the maximum for this length minus 3, at least 1
pipeline.param.denoise.rule: How the threshold λ is chosen per level; σ is estimated from the MAD of d1
pipeline.param.denoise.rule.bayes: BayesShrink: λ = σ²/σx per level, adapts to the signal
pipeline.param.denoise.rule.visu: VisuShrink: λ = σ√(2 ln N), removes nearly all noise but oversmooths
pipeline.param.denoise.rule.sure: SureShrink: λ minimises Stein's unbiased risk estimate per level
pipeline.param.denoise.rule.minimax: Donoho–Johnstone minimax threshold: milder than the universal one
pipeline.param.denoise.mode: Shrinkage function: how coefficients change relative to λ
pipeline.param.denoise.mode.soft: soft: |y| ≤ λ → 0, the rest shrink by λ; smooth but biased
pipeline.param.denoise.mode.hard: hard: |y| ≤ λ → 0, the rest kept; less bias, more residual noise
pipeline.param.denoise.shifts: Circular shifts to average over (cycle spinning): more means fewer artefacts, slower
pipeline.about.thd: Report: fundamental frequency and total harmonic distortion
pipeline.param.thd.harmonics: Highest harmonic counted: the 2nd to Nth below Nyquist enter the THD
pipeline.about.onsets: Report: onset times found from spectral flux, in seconds
pipeline.param.onsets.n: FFT window length, samples: longer is finer in frequency, coarser in time
pipeline.param.onsets.hop: Window hop, samples: smaller gives finer onset times but takes longer
pipeline.about.export: Saves the samples to CSV or JSON and reports what was written
pipeline.param.export.path: File path; a relative path is resolved against the pipeline's folder
pipeline.param.export.format.csv: table: column n plus one column ch0, ch1… per channel
pipeline.param.export.format.json: object {rate, channels: [[…], …]}: the rate and channel arrays
pipeline.about.export_report: Saves the fields of the incoming report to CSV or JSON
pipeline.param.export_report.path: File path; a relative path is resolved against the pipeline's folder
pipeline.param.export_report.format.csv: two columns field,value, one row per field
pipeline.param.export_report.format.json: object with passed and fields (name → value)
pipeline.about.check: Compares a signal with the reference ref and reports pass or fail
pipeline.param.check.kind: Pass criterion; a channel count mismatch or a short input always fails
pipeline.param.check.kind.pr: perfect reconstruction: max|x̂ − x| at most tol
pipeline.param.check.kind.error: error budget: max|x̂ − x| at most tol, for approximate schemes
pipeline.param.check.kind.snr: reconstruction SNR in dB at least tol
pipeline.param.check.tol: Threshold: the largest error for pr and error, the smallest SNR in dB for snr
pipeline.param.check.delay: How far the tested signal lags the reference, in samples, or auto to find it
pipeline.param.check.delay.0: compare without a shift, sample against sample
pipeline.param.check.delay.auto: search lags 0…4096 for the smallest error on channel 0
pipeline.about.wav_out: Writes the signal to a WAV file and reports how many samples clipped
pipeline.param.wav_out.path: File path; a relative path is resolved against the pipeline's folder
pipeline.param.wav_out.bits.f32: 32-bit float: values beyond full scale are kept, not clipped
pipeline.param.wav_out.dither: Dither when rounding to an integer format; ignored for f32
pipeline.param.wav_out.dither.none: plain rounding: the error follows the signal
pipeline.param.wav_out.dither.tpdf: triangular ±1 LSB noise before rounding: the error becomes steady noise
pipeline.param.wav_out.seed: Dither generator seed: the same seed writes the same file
pipeline.about.listen: Listening point: the connected signal can be played from the editor
pipeline.about.pad: Adds zeros before and after the signal
pipeline.param.pad.before: Zeros to insert at the start: samples, or seconds with an s suffix (0.01s)
pipeline.param.pad.after: Zeros to append at the end: samples, or seconds with an s suffix (0.01s)
pipeline.about.concat: Joins two signals: b follows right after a
pipeline.about.multiply: Sample-wise product factor·a·b; without input b, just a·factor
pipeline.param.multiply.factor: Constant factor; a negative value flips the polarity
pipeline.about.window: Multiplies the whole signal by a window of the same length
pipeline.param.window.kind: Window shape: a trade-off between main-lobe width and side-lobe level
pipeline.param.window.kind.hann: Hann: side lobes at −31 dB, a good general choice
pipeline.param.window.kind.hamming: Hamming: first side lobe at −43 dB, but slow roll-off
pipeline.param.window.kind.blackman: Blackman: side lobes at −58 dB, a wider main lobe
pipeline.param.window.kind.kaiser: Kaiser: the shape is set by beta
pipeline.param.window.kind.tukey: Tukey: flat middle with cosine tapers, alpha is their share
pipeline.param.window.beta: Kaiser parameter: higher lowers the side lobes and widens the main lobe; kaiser only
pipeline.param.window.alpha: Share of the length in the Tukey tapers: 0 is rectangular, 1 is Hann; tukey only
pipeline.about.fade: Fades the signal in at the start and out at the end
pipeline.param.fade.fade_in: Fade-in length in samples, or seconds with an s suffix (0.01s); 0 turns it off
pipeline.param.fade.fade_out: Fade-out length in samples, or seconds with an s suffix (0.01s); 0 turns it off
pipeline.param.fade.curve.cosine: raised half-cosine: a gentle start and end of the ramp
pipeline.about.invert: Flips the sign of every sample: x → −x
pipeline.about.abs: Absolute value of each sample: full-wave rectification
pipeline.about.diff: First difference y[n] = x[n] − x[n−1], with x[−1] = 0
pipeline.about.cumsum: Running sum y[n] = x[0] + … + x[n]: a discrete integral
pipeline.about.softclip: Soft clipping y = tanh(drive·x): smooth saturation within ±1
pipeline.param.softclip.drive: Gain before tanh: higher means stronger saturation and distortion
pipeline.about.dc_offset: Adds a constant to every sample
pipeline.param.dc_offset.value: Offset in sample units (1.0 is full scale)
pipeline.about.trim_silence: Trims silence at the start and end, common to all channels
pipeline.param.trim_silence.threshold_db: Silence threshold, dBFS: edges quieter than it in every channel are cut
pipeline.about.add_noise: Adds noise of a chosen colour at a given SNR
pipeline.param.add_noise.color: Noise colour: the slope of its spectrum
pipeline.param.add_noise.color.white: white: equal power at all frequencies
pipeline.param.add_noise.color.pink: pink 1/f: −3 dB per octave, equal power in every octave
pipeline.param.add_noise.color.brown: brown 1/f²: −6 dB per octave, dominated by lows
pipeline.param.add_noise.snr_db: Signal-to-noise ratio, dB, over the mean power of all channels: lower is noisier
pipeline.param.add_noise.seed: Noise generator seed; channel c uses seed + c
pipeline.about.chirp: Chirp: a sine whose frequency glides from f0 to f1
pipeline.param.chirp.method: How the frequency changes over time
pipeline.param.chirp.method.linear: linear: equal Hz per unit time
pipeline.param.chirp.method.log: logarithmic: equal octaves per unit time; f0 and f1 must be above 0
pipeline.param.chirp.f1: End frequency, Hz; below f0 the chirp falls
pipeline.param.chirp.amplitude: Peak amplitude; a negative value flips the polarity
pipeline.param.chirp.rate: Sample rate, Hz; frequencies above half of it alias
pipeline.about.osc: Periodic waveforms: square, sawtooth, triangle or a pulse train
pipeline.param.osc.kind.square: rectangular ±1; duty is the share of the period at +1
pipeline.param.osc.kind.sawtooth: sawtooth: rises from −1 to 1 over width of the period, then falls
pipeline.param.osc.kind.pulses: a unit pulse at the start of every period, zeros in between
pipeline.param.osc.duty: Duty cycle: share of the period at +1; square only
pipeline.param.osc.width: Rising share of the sawtooth period: 1 ramps up, 0 ramps down; sawtooth only
pipeline.param.osc.amplitude: Amplitude; a negative value flips the polarity
pipeline.param.osc.rate: Sample rate, Hz; frequencies above half of it alias
pipeline.about.iir: Classic IIR filter, run as a cascade of biquad sections
pipeline.param.iir.family: Filter family: shape of the magnitude and phase response
pipeline.param.iir.family.butterworth: Butterworth: maximally flat passband, no ripple
pipeline.param.iir.family.cheby1: Chebyshev I: ripple rp in the passband, steeper roll-off
pipeline.param.iir.family.cheby2: Chebyshev II: flat passband, attenuation rs in the stopband
pipeline.param.iir.family.ellip: elliptic: ripple rp and rs, the steepest roll-off for the order
pipeline.param.iir.family.bessel: Bessel: nearly constant group delay, gentle roll-off
pipeline.param.iir.type.bandpass: band-pass: passes between the two cutoff frequencies
pipeline.param.iir.type.bandstop: band-stop: rejects between the two cutoff frequencies
pipeline.param.iir.order: Filter order: higher is steeper but rings longer
pipeline.param.iir.cutoff: Cutoff frequency, Hz; two, space- or comma-separated, for band-pass and band-stop
pipeline.param.iir.rp: Passband ripple, dB; for cheby1 and ellip
pipeline.param.iir.rs: Stopband attenuation, dB; for cheby2 and ellip
pipeline.param.iir.zero_phase: Whether to filter forward and backward (filtfilt) to cancel the phase shift
pipeline.param.iir.zero_phase.no: ordinary causal filtering: delay and phase distortion
pipeline.param.iir.zero_phase.yes: forward and backward: zero phase, squared magnitude, doubled order
pipeline.about.fir: Windowed-sinc FIR filter (as scipy firwin) with linear phase
pipeline.param.fir.numtaps: Number of taps N: more gives a sharper transition but a (N−1)/2-sample delay
pipeline.param.fir.cutoff: Cutoff frequencies, Hz, space- or comma-separated: one for low/high-pass, more for bands
pipeline.param.fir.window: Window used to truncate the ideal response
pipeline.param.fir.window.hamming: Hamming: about 53 dB stopband, the usual choice
pipeline.param.fir.window.blackman: Blackman: about 74 dB stopband, wider transition
pipeline.param.fir.window.kaiser: Kaiser: the attenuation is set by beta
pipeline.param.fir.window.boxcar: rectangular: narrowest transition, only about 21 dB stopband
pipeline.param.fir.beta: Kaiser parameter: higher gives more attenuation and a wider transition; kaiser only
pipeline.param.fir.pass_zero: Whether the filter passes zero frequency (DC)
pipeline.param.fir.pass_zero.yes: DC passes: one cutoff gives low-pass, two give band-stop
pipeline.param.fir.pass_zero.no: DC is blocked: one cutoff gives high-pass, two give band-pass
pipeline.param.fir.compensate: Whether to remove the filter's (N−1)/2-sample group delay
pipeline.param.fir.compensate.no: output lags by (N−1)/2 samples, like a real causal filter
pipeline.param.fir.compensate.yes: output shifted back by (N−1)/2, time-aligned with the input
pipeline.about.median: Median filter: each sample becomes the median of its window; removes clicks
pipeline.param.median.kernel: Window length, odd, samples: longer removes wider spikes and smooths more
pipeline.about.moving_average: Moving average over length samples: the simplest low-pass
pipeline.param.moving_average.length: Averaging window, samples: longer smooths more
pipeline.param.moving_average.centred: Whether to centre the window, removing the (length−1)/2 delay
pipeline.param.moving_average.centred.no: causal window over past samples: output lags by (length−1)/2
pipeline.param.moving_average.centred.ye: window around the current sample: no lag
pipeline.about.preemphasis: Pre-emphasis y[n] = x[n] − k·x[n−1]: boosts high frequencies
pipeline.param.preemphasis.coeff: Coefficient k: closer to 1 boosts highs and cuts lows more
pipeline.about.deemphasis: De-emphasis y[n] = x[n] + k·y[n−1]: undoes preemphasis
pipeline.param.deemphasis.coeff: Coefficient k, the same as in pre-emphasis; closer to 1 means longer memory
pipeline.about.lift97: 9/7 (CDF, JPEG 2000) wavelet via lifting: multilevel decomposition
pipeline.param.lift97.levels: Number of levels; the signal needs at least 2^levels samples
pipeline.about.ilift97: Inverse 9/7 lifting: rebuilds the signal from lift97 bands
pipeline.about.mra: MRA component: one band's contribution brought back to the time domain
pipeline.param.mra.component: Band to keep: a (or aJ) for the approximation, dJ for the details of level J
pipeline.param.mra.component.a: approximation aJ: the coarse low-frequency part
pipeline.param.mra.component.d: details of level J: roughly the band fs/2^(J+1)…fs/2^J
pipeline.about.merge: Builds a multichannel signal: the channels of l, then those of r
pipeline.about.swap: Swaps channels 0 and 1, left and right
pipeline.about.pan: Panning: mixes to mono and places it in stereo at position
pipeline.param.pan.position: Position: −1 is hard left, 0 centre, 1 hard right
pipeline.param.pan.law: Pan law: how the level splits between L and R
pipeline.param.pan.law.constant_power: constant power: L = cos, R = sin; −3 dB each at centre
pipeline.param.pan.law.linear: linear: L = (1−p)/2, R = (1+p)/2; −6 dB each at centre
pipeline.about.duplicate: Repeats channels cyclically up to the requested count
pipeline.param.duplicate.channels: Number of output channels; input channels repeat cyclically
pipeline.about.stats: Report: RMS, peak, crest factor, mean, std, zero crossings, spectral centroid
pipeline.about.loudness: Report: the largest and mean RMS level over sliding windows, dBFS
pipeline.param.loudness.window: Window length in samples, or seconds with an s suffix (0.01s)
pipeline.param.loudness.hop: Window hop in samples, or seconds with an s suffix (0.01s); smaller is denser
pipeline.about.lms: Adaptive LMS/NLMS FIR filter: predicts d from x, outputs error e and estimate y
pipeline.param.lms.taps: Filter length, taps: more models a longer path but converges slower
pipeline.param.lms.mu: Step size: larger converges faster but noisier; too large makes LMS diverge
pipeline.param.lms.rule.nlms: normalised LMS: step divided by the energy of x, stable for mu < 2
pipeline.param.lms.rule.lms: classic LMS: unnormalised step that depends on the level of x
pipeline.about.wiener: Local Wiener filter: smooths where the local variance is close to the noise
pipeline.param.wiener.size: Window for the local mean and variance, samples: larger smooths more
pipeline.param.wiener.noise: Noise variance; 0 estimates it as the mean local variance
pipeline.about.spectral_subtract: Spectral subtraction: removes the noise power estimate from each STFT frame
pipeline.param.spectral_subtract.alpha: Over-subtraction factor: higher removes more noise but distorts more
pipeline.param.spectral_subtract.beta: Spectral floor: the share of noise power a bin never drops below
pipeline.param.spectral_subtract.n: FFT frame length, samples, hop n/4: longer is finer in frequency, coarser in time
pipeline.param.spectral_subtract.noise_s: Without a noise input, how many seconds at the start count as noise
pipeline.about.deconvolve: Wiener deconvolution: recovers x from y = h ∗ x given h
pipeline.param.deconvolve.snr_db: Expected SNR, dB: higher inverts more boldly but amplifies more noise
pipeline.about.polyphase: Splits the signal into its polyphase components x[2n] and x[2n+1] at half the rate
pipeline.about.ipolyphase: Interleaves even and odd back into one signal at twice the rate
pipeline.about.wpt: Wavelet packet decomposition: also splits the details, keeps the chosen basis
pipeline.param.wpt.wavelet: Wavelet for every split; an orthogonal one keeps the energy and suits the best basis
pipeline.param.wpt.levels: Depth J of the full tree; the signal needs at least 2^J samples
pipeline.param.wpt.basis: Which leaves of the tree to output, in frequency order
pipeline.param.wpt.basis.best: Coifman–Wickerhauser best basis by Shannon entropy, one for all channels
pipeline.param.wpt.basis.full: all 2^J nodes of the deepest level: equal bands
pipeline.param.wpt.basis.dwt: aJ and dJ…d1: the same tiling as an ordinary DWT
pipeline.param.wpt.ext: Signal extension at the edges, as in pywt
pipeline.param.wpt.ext.symmetric: mirror repeating the edge: … x1 x0 | x0 x1 …
pipeline.param.wpt.ext.smooth: linear extrapolation from the two edge samples
pipeline.param.wpt.ext.reflect: mirror without repeating the edge: … x2 x1 | x0 x1 x2 …
pipeline.param.wpt.ext.antisymmetric: mirror with a sign flip: … −x1 −x0 | x0 x1 …
pipeline.param.wpt.ext.antireflect: point reflection about the edge sample: x[−n] = 2x0 − x[n]
pipeline.about.iwpt: Rebuilds the signal from wpt bands using the basis they carry
pipeline.about.keep_largest: Keeps the K largest detail coefficients by magnitude and zeros the rest
pipeline.param.keep_largest.mode: How amount sets K: a share of the coefficients or their number
pipeline.param.keep_largest.mode.percent: K is amount percent of the coefficients in the pool
pipeline.param.keep_largest.mode.count: K is amount itself, rounded to a whole number
pipeline.param.keep_largest.amount: Percentage or count of coefficients kept in each channel
pipeline.param.keep_largest.keep_approx: Whether the approximation is kept whole and left out of the selection
approximation kept whole, K is chosen among the details
approximation competes with the details for the K places
pipeline.about.coeff_quantize: Uniform mid-tread quantization of the details: c → Δ·round(c/Δ)
pipeline.param.coeff_quantize.mode: How the step Δ is set
pipeline.param.coeff_quantize.mode.step: one step Δ = step for every detail band
pipeline.param.coeff_quantize.bits: Bits per coefficient, sign included: fewer bits mean a coarser step
pipeline.param.coeff_quantize.step: Quantizer step Δ in coefficient units; values below Δ/2 become zero
pipeline.about.shift: Shifts the signal in time by whole samples; the length stays the same
pipeline.param.shift.samples: Shift in samples: positive delays the signal, negative advances it
pipeline.param.shift.mode.zero: zeros enter, samples pushed past the edge are lost
pipeline.param.shift.mode.circular: circular shift: samples leaving one end come back at the other
pipeline.about.biquad: Second-order section from the RBJ Audio EQ Cookbook
pipeline.param.biquad.type: Filter type; the cookbook formula for b and a
pipeline.param.biquad.type.lowpass: low-pass: −3 dB at f0 for q = 0.7071
pipeline.param.biquad.type.highpass: high-pass: −3 dB at f0 for q = 0.7071
pipeline.param.biquad.type.bandpass: band-pass with 0 dB at f0; q sets the width
pipeline.param.biquad.type.notch: notch: zero gain at f0, q sets the width
pipeline.param.biquad.type.peaking: peaking EQ: gain_db at f0, 0 dB far from it
pipeline.param.biquad.type.allpass: all-pass: flat magnitude, the phase turns by 360° around f0
pipeline.param.biquad.f0: Centre or corner frequency, Hz; must lie between 0 and Nyquist
pipeline.param.biquad.q: Quality factor: higher is narrower and more resonant
pipeline.param.biquad.gain_db: Gain at f0 or on the shelf, dB; for peaking, lowshelf and highshelf only
pipeline.about.compressor: Feed-forward compressor: lowers the level above threshold by ratio
pipeline.param.compressor.detector: How the level is measured; channels are linked by one gain
pipeline.param.compressor.detector.rms: mean square over all channels, averaged over rms_ms
pipeline.param.compressor.threshold_db: Threshold, dBFS: the level above which compression starts
pipeline.param.compressor.ratio: Compression ratio: 4 means 4 dB over threshold become 1 dB
pipeline.param.compressor.knee_db: Knee width, dB: 0 is a hard knee, more makes the onset gradual
pipeline.param.compressor.attack_ms: Attack time constant, ms: how fast the gain drops when the level rises
pipeline.param.compressor.release_ms: Release time constant, ms: how fast the gain recovers when the level falls
pipeline.param.compressor.makeup_db: Makeup gain, dB, added after compression
pipeline.param.compressor.rms_ms: Averaging time of the RMS detector, ms; rms only
pipeline.about.limiter: Peak limiter: a compressor with an infinite ratio and a hard knee
pipeline.param.limiter.threshold_db: Ceiling, dBFS: with attack 0 no sample ends above it
pipeline.param.limiter.attack_ms: Attack time constant, ms: above 0 short peaks slip past the ceiling
pipeline.param.limiter.release_ms: Release time constant, ms: how fast the gain recovers after a peak
pipeline.about.gate: Noise gate: attenuates the signal while its peak stays below the threshold
pipeline.param.gate.threshold_db: Threshold, dBFS: below it the gate closes
pipeline.param.gate.range_db: Attenuation of the closed gate, dB: 80 is nearly silence
pipeline.param.gate.attack_ms: Opening time constant, ms: how fast the gate opens on a loud sound
pipeline.param.gate.release_ms: Closing time constant, ms: how fast the gate closes after it
pipeline.about.echo: Echo with feedback: repeats every delay_ms, each feedback times quieter
pipeline.param.echo.feedback: Share of each repeat fed back: 0 gives one echo, near 1 a long tail
pipeline.param.echo.mix: Wet share: 0 is the dry signal only, 1 the echoes only
pipeline.about.comb: Comb filter: the signal plus gain times itself delayed by delay samples
pipeline.param.comb.kind.feedback: y[n] = x[n] + g·y[n−D]: resonant peaks, an IIR filter
pipeline.param.comb.kind.feedforward: y[n] = x[n] + g·x[n−D]: evenly spaced notches, an FIR filter
pipeline.param.comb.delay: Delay D in samples, or seconds with an s suffix (0.01s); at least one sample
pipeline.param.comb.gain: Gain g of the delayed path; feedback needs |g| < 1
pipeline.about.mix: Mixes signals a and b with their gains, or crossfades from a to b
pipeline.param.mix.mode: How the inputs are combined; the shorter one is zero-padded
pipeline.param.mix.mode.sum: sum of both inputs at every sample
pipeline.param.mix.mode.crossfade: a until at, a linear fade over crossfade_ms, then b
pipeline.param.mix.at: Start of the crossfade, s; crossfade only
pipeline.param.mix.crossfade_ms: Crossfade length, ms; 0 switches at once; crossfade only
pipeline.about.lpc: Linear prediction by the autocorrelation method and Levinson–Durbin
pipeline.param.lpc.order: Predictor order p: how many past samples predict the next one
pipeline.about.lpc_synth: All-pole synthesis 1/A(z): rebuilds the signal from residual and report
pipeline.about.spectrum_peaks: Report: the strongest peaks of the Welch spectrum, Hz and dB
pipeline.param.spectrum_peaks.count: How many of the strongest peaks to report
pipeline.param.spectrum_peaks.segment: Welch segment, samples, overlap 50 %: longer resolves closer peaks
pipeline.param.spectrum_peaks.prominence: Minimum prominence, dB: how far a peak must rise above its surroundings
pipeline.about.band_power: Report: share of the power in each octave or third-octave band
pipeline.param.band_power.bands: Band width; centres are the IEC 61260 base-10 series around 1 kHz
pipeline.param.band_power.bands.octave: octave bands from 31.5 Hz to 16 kHz
pipeline.param.band_power.bands.third: third-octave bands from 25 Hz to 20 kHz
pipeline.param.band_power.segment: Welch segment, samples, overlap 50 %: longer resolves the low bands better
pipeline.about.lfilter: Any b, a filter like scipy lfilter; poles outside the unit circle are refused
pipeline.param.lfilter.b: Numerator coefficients b0 b1 …, space- or comma-separated; divided by a0
pipeline.param.lfilter.a: Denominator coefficients a0 a1 …; a0 must not be zero, a lone 1 gives an FIR filter
pipeline.about.fir_taps: Convolves with the given taps like numpy convolve, cut to the input length
pipeline.param.fir_taps.taps: Impulse response h0 h1 …, space- or comma-separated
pipeline.param.fir_taps.compensate: Whether to remove the (N−1)/2-sample delay of an N-tap filter
pipeline.param.fir_taps.compensate.no: output lags by (N−1)/2 samples, like a real causal filter
pipeline.param.fir_taps.compensate.yes: output shifted back by (N−1)/2, time-aligned with the input
pipeline.about.savgol: Least-squares polynomial fit in a sliding window, like scipy savgol_filter
pipeline.param.savgol.window: Window length in samples, odd: longer smooths more
pipeline.param.savgol.polyorder: Polynomial order, below the window: higher keeps peaks sharper but smooths less
pipeline.param.savgol.deriv: Derivative order: 0 smooths, 1 gives the slope per second, 2 the curvature
pipeline.param.savgol.mode: How the window is filled past the ends of the signal
pipeline.param.savgol.mode.interp: fit a polynomial to the first and last window instead of padding
pipeline.param.savgol.mode.mirror: reflect about the end samples without repeating them
pipeline.param.savgol.mode.wrap: continue periodically from the other end
pipeline.about.hilbert: Imaginary part or phase of the analytic signal, like scipy hilbert
pipeline.param.hilbert.output: What to output; the magnitude is the envelope block, the phase rate is inst_freq
pipeline.param.hilbert.output.imag: the Hilbert transform itself: the signal shifted by 90°
pipeline.param.hilbert.output.phase: instantaneous phase in radians, wrapped to −π…π
pipeline.param.hilbert.output.unwrapped: instantaneous phase without 2π jumps, like numpy unwrap
pipeline.about.remez: Designs a minimax FIR by Parks–McClellan, like scipy remez, and applies it
pipeline.param.remez.numtaps: Number of taps N: more gives a sharper transition but a (N−1)/2-sample delay
pipeline.param.remez.bands: Band edges in Hz in pairs, from 0 up to nyquist, e.g. 0 1000 1500 nyquist
pipeline.param.remez.desired: Wanted gain in each band, one value per pair of edges
pipeline.param.remez.weight: Error weight per band, empty means equal; larger makes that band flatter
pipeline.param.remez.type.bandpass: ordinary filter: low-, high-, band-pass or band-stop by the bands
pipeline.param.remez.type.differentiator: gain grows with frequency: a derivative over the bands
pipeline.param.remez.type.hilbert: 90° phase shifter, an FIR Hilbert transformer
pipeline.param.remez.compensate: Whether to remove the (N−1)/2-sample delay of an N-tap filter
pipeline.param.remez.compensate.no: output lags by (N−1)/2 samples, like a real causal filter
pipeline.param.remez.compensate.yes: output shifted back by (N−1)/2, time-aligned with the input
pipeline.about.firls: Designs an FIR by least squares, like scipy firls, and applies it
pipeline.param.firls.numtaps: Number of taps N, odd: more gives a sharper transition but a (N−1)/2-sample delay
pipeline.param.firls.bands: Band edges in Hz in pairs, from 0 up to nyquist, e.g. 0 1000 1500 nyquist
pipeline.param.firls.desired: Wanted gain at every band edge; the gain is linear in between
pipeline.param.firls.weight: Error weight per band, empty means equal; larger fits that band closer
pipeline.param.firls.compensate: Whether to remove the (N−1)/2-sample delay of an N-tap filter
pipeline.param.firls.compensate.no: output lags by (N−1)/2 samples, like a real causal filter
pipeline.param.firls.compensate.yes: output shifted back by (N−1)/2, time-aligned with the input
pipeline.about.pitch: Fundamental frequency per frame by YIN; reports the median and the voiced share
pipeline.param.pitch.fmin: Lowest pitch to look for, Hz: lower needs a longer frame
pipeline.param.pitch.fmax: Highest pitch to look for, Hz
pipeline.param.pitch.frame: Frame length in samples; its first half is the comparison window
pipeline.param.pitch.hop: Step between frames in samples; the f0 output runs at rate/hop
pipeline.param.pitch.threshold: Threshold on the normalised difference: lower is stricter, more frames unvoiced
pipeline.about.mfcc: Mean mel-frequency cepstral coefficients: HTK mel bank, dB, orthonormal DCT-II
pipeline.param.mfcc.n_mfcc: How many coefficients to report, starting with c0, the overall level
pipeline.param.mfcc.n_mels: Number of triangular mel filters from 0 Hz to Nyquist
pipeline.param.mfcc.frame: Frame length in samples, Hann window
pipeline.about.spectral_features: Mean spectral centroid, spread, rolloff, flatness and flux over Hann frames
pipeline.param.spectral_features.frame: Frame length in samples, Hann window: longer is finer in frequency
pipeline.param.spectral_features.rolloff: Rolloff is the frequency below which this percentage of the magnitudes lies
pipeline.about.histogram: Counts samples in equal bins like numpy histogram; the last bin keeps its right edge
pipeline.param.histogram.range: auto takes the signal's minimum and maximum, or give two numbers lo hi
pipeline.about.delay_estimate: Lag of b behind a by the cross-correlation peak, refined between samples
pipeline.about.correlation: Pearson, Spearman and cosine similarity of a and b over their common length
pipeline.about.coeff_stats: Per band: energy share, Shannon entropy in bits, share of near-zero coefficients
pipeline.param.coeff_stats.tol: A coefficient counts as near zero below tol × the largest magnitude in the channel
pipeline.error.too_many_coeffs: {block}: {param} has {n} coefficients, at most {max} are allowed
pipeline.error.a0_zero: lfilter: a[0] must not be zero — every coefficient is divided by it
pipeline.error.lfilter_unstable: lfilter: the denominator has a pole of modulus {r} outside the unit circle — the output would grow without bound
pipeline.error.needs_rate: {block}: the sample rate must be above zero
pipeline.error.band_edge: {block}: the band edge {f} Hz must lie from 0 to the Nyquist frequency {nyquist} Hz
pipeline.error.savgol_window: savgol: window = {value}: the window length must be odd
pipeline.error.savgol_order: savgol: polyorder {order} must be below the window {window}, and deriv {deriv} must not exceed polyorder
pipeline.error.savgol_short: savgol: interp needs at least {window} samples, the input has {n} — pick another mode or a shorter window
pipeline.error.input_not_finite: {block}: the input has samples that are not finite (NaN or infinity)
pipeline.error.delay_short: {block}: the delay is shorter than one sample at this sample rate
pipeline.error.comb_feedback: comb: with kind = feedback the gain must stay below 1 in magnitude, or the filter is unstable
pipeline.error.lpc_order: lpc: order = {order} is too high for this signal — the prediction error reaches zero; lower the order

pipeline.error.lpc_channels: lpc_synth: the report holds coefficients for {report} channels, the residual has {residual}
pipeline.error.pitch_range: pitch: fmin {fmin} Hz must be below fmax {fmax} Hz
pipeline.error.pitch_frame: pitch: frame {frame} is too short for fmin {fmin} Hz at {rate} Hz — it needs at least {min} samples
pipeline.error.mfcc_count: mfcc: n_mfcc {n} must not exceed n_mels {mels}
pipeline.error.histogram_range: histogram: range = {value}: auto or two numbers lo hi with lo below hi are expected
pipeline.about.tremolo: Tremolo: modulates the level periodically at rate_hz
pipeline.param.tremolo.rate_hz: Level modulation frequency, Hz: 2–10 Hz is a classic tremolo
pipeline.param.tremolo.depth: Depth: 0 leaves the signal unchanged, 1 dips the level to zero
pipeline.param.tremolo.shape: Shape of the low-frequency oscillator (LFO) that sets the level
pipeline.param.tremolo.shape.triangle: triangle: a linear rise and fall
pipeline.param.tremolo.shape.square: square: hard switching between the full and the reduced level
pipeline.about.modulated_delay: Chorus, flanger or vibrato: a delay swept by an LFO
pipeline.param.modulated_delay.mode: Effect: how the delayed and the original signals combine
pipeline.param.modulated_delay.mode.chor: chorus: a 10–30 ms delay mixed with the original, no feedback
pipeline.param.modulated_delay.mode.flan: flanger: a 0–5 ms delay with feedback, a comb of sweeping notches
pipeline.param.modulated_delay.mode.vibr: vibrato: the delayed signal alone, so the pitch wobbles
pipeline.param.modulated_delay.rate_hz: LFO frequency, Hz: how fast the delay sweeps
pipeline.param.modulated_delay.depth_ms: Sweep width, ms: the delay moves from base_ms to base_ms + depth_ms
pipeline.param.modulated_delay.base_ms: Shortest delay, ms; it never gets shorter than one sample
pipeline.param.modulated_delay.feedback: Share of the delayed signal fed back into the delay; flanger only
pipeline.param.modulated_delay.mix: Share of the delayed signal in the output: 0 is dry only; vibrato always uses 1
pipeline.about.phaser: Phaser: a chain of allpass stages whose notches an LFO sweeps across the spectrum
pipeline.param.phaser.stages: Number of first-order allpass stages: every two give one notch in the response
pipeline.param.phaser.rate_hz: LFO frequency, Hz: how fast the notches move
pipeline.param.phaser.min_hz: Lower end of the stages' break-frequency sweep, Hz; below Nyquist
pipeline.param.phaser.max_hz: Upper end of the sweep, Hz; below Nyquist; the sweep is even in octaves
pipeline.param.phaser.feedback: Share of the chain output fed back to its input: sharper notches, more resonance
pipeline.param.phaser.mix: Share of the processed signal in the output: 0.5 gives the deepest notches
pipeline.about.reverb: Freeverb reverb: damped comb filters followed by allpass stages
pipeline.param.reverb.room_size: Room size: larger means a longer tail (comb feedback 0.7…0.98)
pipeline.param.reverb.damping: High-frequency damping in the tail: higher sounds darker
pipeline.param.reverb.wet: Level of the reverberation; the input length is kept, so pad it to hear the tail
pipeline.param.reverb.dry: Level of the original signal in the output
pipeline.about.wavefold: Wavefolder: whatever exceeds ±1 is reflected back inside
pipeline.param.wavefold.drive: Gain before folding: higher gives more folds and overtones
pipeline.param.wavefold.shape.triangle: reflection off ±1: a triangular transfer curve
pipeline.about.am: AM: y = (1 + depth·x)·cos(2π·carrier_hz·t); the input is the message
pipeline.param.am.carrier_hz: Carrier frequency, Hz; above half the sample rate it aliases
pipeline.param.am.depth: Modulation index: where |depth·x| > 1 the envelope crosses zero (overmodulation)
pipeline.about.fm: FM: instantaneous frequency carrier_hz + deviation_hz·x; the input is the message
pipeline.param.fm.carrier_hz: Carrier frequency, Hz; above half the sample rate it aliases
pipeline.param.fm.deviation_hz: Frequency deviation per unit of input, Hz: how far the frequency swings
pipeline.param.gausspulse.bw: Fractional bandwidth at level bwr, a share of fc: smaller gives a longer pulse
pipeline.param.gausspulse.bwr: Level at which the bandwidth is measured, dB; negative
pipeline.param.gausspulse.amplitude: Peak amplitude; a negative value flips the polarity
pipeline.param.gausspulse.rate: Sample rate, Hz; frequencies above half of it alias
pipeline.param.gausspulse.duration: Signal length, s; the pulse sits in the middle
pipeline.about.impulse_train: Unit impulses every period samples, with zeros in between
pipeline.param.impulse_train.period: Period in samples, or seconds with an s suffix (0.01s)
pipeline.param.impulse_train.offset: Position of the first impulse: samples, or seconds with an s suffix
pipeline.param.impulse_train.amplitude: Impulse height; a negative value flips the polarity
pipeline.about.affine: y = scale·x + offset: scale and shift in one step
pipeline.param.affine.scale: Multiplier; a negative value flips the polarity
pipeline.about.math: Sample-wise function: logarithm, exponential, root, power, sign, 1/x
pipeline.param.math.op: Function; outside its domain the block stops with an error instead of giving NaN
pipeline.param.math.op.log: natural logarithm ln x; needs x > 0
pipeline.param.math.op.log10: base-10 logarithm; needs x > 0; 20·log10 of the magnitude is the level in dB
pipeline.param.math.op.pow: power xᵖ; for x < 0 p must be whole, for x = 0 not negative
pipeline.about.binary: Sample-wise operation on a and b: divide, min, max, power, hypotenuse
pipeline.param.binary.op: Operation; the shorter input is padded with zeros, as in add
pipeline.param.binary.op.divide: a / b; a zero in b, padding included, is an error
pipeline.param.binary.op.min: the smaller of a and b
pipeline.param.binary.op.max: the larger of a and b
pipeline.param.binary.op.pow: aᵇ; for a < 0 b must be whole, for a = 0 not negative
pipeline.param.binary.op.hypot: √(a² + b²) without overflow: the magnitude of two components
pipeline.about.repeat: Repeats the whole signal back to back: times copies in all
pipeline.param.repeat.times: How many copies the output holds; 1 leaves the signal as is
pipeline.about.select_channel: Keeps the one channel with number index
pipeline.param.select_channel.index: Channel number from zero: 0 is left, 1 is right
pipeline.about.channel_delay: Shifts each channel by its own number of samples; the length is kept
pipeline.param.channel_delay.delays: Channel delays in samples, space- or comma-separated: 0 12; the last repeats, a negative one advances
pipeline.about.stereo_width: Stereo width via mid/side: the side signal is scaled by width
pipeline.param.stereo_width.width: Side-signal factor: 0 is mono, 1 changes nothing, 2 is twice as wide
pipeline.param.balance.position: Position p: −1 keeps the left only (+3 dB), 0 changes nothing, 1 keeps the right only
pipeline.about.sample_hold: Sample and hold: every hold-th sample is held until the next; the length is kept
pipeline.param.sample_hold.hold: Hold length: samples, or seconds with an s suffix; the effective rate drops to fs/hold
pipeline.about.dc_block: First-order high-pass y[n] = x[n] − x[n−1] + r·y[n−1]: removes DC
pipeline.about.time_stretch: Changes the duration and keeps the pitch: rate = 2 is twice as fast and short, 0.5 twice as slow
pipeline.about.pitch_shift: Shifts the pitch by n semitones and keeps the duration: stretch by 2^(n/12), then resample back
pipeline.about.speed: Changes the speed like a record: tempo and pitch together; rate = 2 is twice as fast and an octave higher
pipeline.param.dc_block.r: Pole: closer to 1 lowers the cutoff, about (1−r)·fs/2π, and slows settling
pipeline.param.time_stretch.rate: How many times faster: above 1 is shorter, below 1 longer; the pitch stays
pipeline.param.pitch_shift.semitones: Shift in semitones, fractions allowed: 12 is an octave up, −12 an octave down, 7 a fifth
pipeline.param.speed.rate: How many times faster; the pitch moves with the speed: 2 is an octave up, 0.5 an octave down
pipeline.param.time_stretch.method.vocod: phase vocoder as in librosa: STFT magnitudes are interpolated, phases accumulated; smooth on tones, smears transients
pipeline.param.time_stretch.method.locke: vocoder with phase locking (Laroche–Dolson): bins around a peak take the peak's phase — less phasiness, a fuller sound
pipeline.param.time_stretch.method.wsola: WSOLA in time: signal pieces shift within hop to join by shape; keeps transients, good for a single voice
pipeline.param.time_stretch.n_fft: STFT window length (the piece length for WSOLA), samples, even: longer is sharper in frequency, blurrier in time
pipeline.param.time_stretch.hop: Window step, samples, at most n_fft/2: smaller is smoother and slower; for WSOLA also the piece shift limit
pipeline.param.pitch_shift.method.vocode: phase vocoder as in librosa: STFT magnitudes are interpolated, phases accumulated; smooth on tones, smears transients
pipeline.param.pitch_shift.method.locked: vocoder with phase locking (Laroche–Dolson): bins around a peak take the peak's phase — less phasiness, a fuller sound
pipeline.param.pitch_shift.method.wsola: WSOLA in time: signal pieces shift within hop to join by shape; keeps transients, good for a single voice
pipeline.param.pitch_shift.n_fft: STFT window length (the piece length for WSOLA), samples, even: longer is sharper in frequency, blurrier in time
pipeline.param.pitch_shift.hop: Window step, samples, at most n_fft/2: smaller is smoother and slower; for WSOLA also the piece shift limit
pipeline.error.no_rate: {block}: the input has no sample rate, so hertz and milliseconds mean nothing
pipeline.error.rate_too_high: {block}: the sample rate {rate} Hz is too high — the block's delays and windows would not fit in memory
pipeline.error.stretch_window: {block}: the window n_fft = {n_fft} must be even and the hop = {hop} at most n_fft/2

pipeline.error.binary_domain: binary: {op} is undefined at sample {index} of channel {channel}, where a = {a}, b = {b}
pipeline.error.select_channel: select_channel: there is no channel {index}, the input has {n}
pipeline.error.needs_stereo: {block}: at least two channels are needed, the input has {n}
pipeline.error.channel_delay: channel_delay: delays = {value}: whole sample counts are expected, e.g. 0 12
